mapping.note: Maps record kinds, link relations and record fields to RDF. Fields with a scheme hold concept keys from data/vocab/<scheme>.ttl and export as concept IRIs. An external term is used only where its meaning matches; everything else is in the rewire vocabulary. Changes to this file are reviewed like record changes.

method.basis: A described procedure, independent of a trained artifact (W3C ML Schema Algorithm).

model.basis: A named model or model family as released. Most model records are families, which are neither executable implementations (mls:Implementation) nor trained artifacts (mls:Model), so no external class is asserted.

configuration.basis: The exact setup that produced scores. Many are reported labels, paper comparators or score-threshold schemes rather than trained artifacts, so mls:Model is not asserted.

pipeline.basis: A multi-stage system; its results are not results of any model it uses.

service.basis: A hosted service with its own terms and limits.

benchmark.basis: No external class matches a benchmark suite as used here.

task.basis: Linking to EDAM Operation needs a reviewed per-task mapping; not yet done.

protocol.basis: OBI protocol: a plan specification of how to carry out a process.

evaluator.basis: Scoring software such as AMBER, OPAL or PoseBusters; not an implementation of a machine-learning algorithm.

dataset_subset.basis: A defined subset is itself a dataset.

baseline.basis: A proposed or source-supported comparison procedure; no external class matches.

evaluation.basis: One execution of a configuration under a protocol, as reported.

result.basis: ML Schema ModelEvaluation holds one measured value of an evaluation measure.

source.basis: Paper, supplement, repository file or web page. A finer schema.org type needs a reviewed per-source field.

claim.basis: One sourced assertion about another record; its sources via dcterms:source.

use_case.basis: A research or clinical decision question with its intended users, available inputs, desired output and setting. No external class matches: IAO objective specification (IAO_0000005) and plan specification (IAO_0000104) are directives realised by processes, schema:Question is a subclass of Comment, and NCIT Use Case (C81930) is a software interaction script.

system.basis: Evaluation to the configuration, model, method, pipeline or service it evaluated. Not inherited by families.

assessment.basis: Evaluation to the task, protocol or benchmark it was assessed on.

data.basis: Evaluation to the dataset or dataset subset it used.

original_evaluation.basis: A copied result to the evaluation it was copied from.

implemented_by.basis: Baseline to the configuration, model or method that implements it.

measured_in.basis: Baseline to an evaluation that measured it as a comparator; the values belong to that evaluation's results.

uses_data.basis: Task, protocol or baseline to the data it uses.

used_in.basis: Dataset subset to the protocol that uses it.

family.basis: Configuration or variant to its model family. Results roll up only when a claim backs the link.

variant_of.basis: Model to the model it is a variant of. Not transitive.

configuration_of.basis: Configuration to the model, method or pipeline it configures.

alias_of.basis: Same identity under another ID. Deliberately not owl:sameAs, which would merge results without review.

uses_model.basis: A pipeline or service depends on a model. Not transitive and not a subproperty of rb:evaluatedSubject: pipeline results are never results of the model.

part_of.basis: Component of a suite. A subproperty of dcterms:isPartOf and of the transitive rb:within, so the transitivity applies only to rewire part-of links.

evaluates_task.basis: Resource to the task it evaluates.

applicable_to.basis: Candidate applicability; not evidence of performance.

same_data_as.basis: Informational data reuse; never merges results.

companion_of.basis: Source to the paper it belongs with: its repository, leaderboard, supplement or another version of the paper. The discrepancy rules treat both as one study (docs/discrepancies.md). Never merges results.

assessed_by.basis: Use case to a protocol that a relevance judgement claim grades for it. Every asserted link is exported, including those whose judgement is still a draft; the claim's status and grade decide whether its evaluations count as evidence. Not a subproperty of rb:testedOn and in no property chain, so no result is inferred to belong to a use case. No external property starts from a question: the domain of SEPIO has_evidence (SEPIO_0000189) is a proposition or assertion, and oa:hasTarget starts from an annotation.

supersedes.basis: A newer record replacing an older one.

subject.basis: Claim to the record it is about.

source.basis: Record to a source it is derived from.

source_ids.basis: The source the record (a description) is taken from. prov:wasDerivedFrom would make every described thing, including evaluation runs, a prov:Entity derived from a paper.

ops.summary: Run and evaluate the supplied BEELINE GSD example configuration, then generate AUPRC/AUROC plots.
prerequisites: Git, conda and a functioning Docker installation; the repository executes supported algorithms in containers.
The supplied config-files/config.yaml expects GSD expression, pseudotime and ground-truth files under inputs/example/GSD. Verify the local data layout before running.

steps.title: Check out the reviewed repository
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/Murali-group/Beeline.git
cd Beeline
git checkout --detach 37464085eb8a95d6cc6a3d3a3c649d36db6052ed
steps.explanation: Repository checkout wrapper: the detached revision selects the exact official source inspected for this guide.

steps.title: Set up the environment and algorithm images
steps.shell:
bash utils/setupAnacondaVENV.sh
bash utils/initialize.sh
conda activate BEELINE
steps.explanation: These setup commands use the official default image-pull behavior. Conda must already be initialized in the shell; the README illustrates a Miniconda-specific initialization path.

steps.title: Run the configured algorithms
steps.explanation: This executes the algorithms and datasets enabled by the YAML file. The README points to a missing VSC file; this guide explicitly substitutes the supplied GSD example config, so it is a different example dataset.

steps.title: Evaluate and plot ROC/precision-recall performance
steps.shell:
python BLEvaluator.py -c config-files/config.yaml -a
python BLPlotter.py -c config-files/config.yaml -o ./plots -a -r
steps.explanation: The flags are selected from the official tables: evaluator -a computes AUPRC/AUROC; plotter -a and -r produce their corresponding figures. The README points to a missing VSC file; this guide explicitly substitutes the supplied GSD example config, so it is a different example dataset.

outputs: Ranked edges under outputs/example_run_GSD/GSD/<run_id>/<algorithm_id>/rankedEdges.csv, using output_settings in the supplied config.
AUPRC and AUROC plot files under ./plots in PDF and PNG formats.
limitations: The README VSC command references a configuration absent from the pinned repository. This guide uses the checked-in GSD example instead and does not claim VSC results.
The Docker tags are not image-digest pinned by the README; this code revision alone does not freeze algorithm containers.
Ground-truth network availability and matching input/configuration paths are prerequisites; no data-download command is invented.
The inspected instructions do not establish a minimum RAM/VRAM requirement, wall-clock runtime or monetary cost; none is inferred.

ops.summary: ATOM3D provides molecular-structure datasets and utilities for task-specific evaluation.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: ATOM3D evaluates predictions from molecular structures using eight separate tasks. It supplies task-specific reference labels and partitions, ranging from random small molecules to held-out protein families and future structure-prediction targets. Each task has its own metric and representation-matched baseline; the suite is not a single universal structure score.

facts.label: Datasets
facts.value: Three-dimensional molecular data with associated labels/metadata; ligand-binding affinity is one documented example.
facts.source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

facts.label: Splits
facts.value: Task-specific: random molecules for SMP; 30% protein sequence identity for PIP, MSP and the strict LBA split; CATH topology groups for RES; protein targets for LEP; competition years for PSR and RSR. LBA also provides a less restrictive 60% identity split.
facts.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: SMP: MAE; PIP/MSP/LEP: classification AUROC; RES: accuracy; LBA: RMSE and correlations; PSR/RSR: correlations of predicted structure quality with reference GDT_TS/RMSD. Metrics and aggregation belong to each task.
facts.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

facts.label: Baselines
facts.value: 3D CNNs, graph networks and equivariant networks are compared with task-specific 1D/2D methods; structure-ranking tasks also use established 3D methods. Appendix F documents the per-task comparators.
facts.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: Protein-sequence, topology, target and temporal partitions reduce task-specific overlap; PIP prunes DIPS proteins against DB5. SMP uses a random molecular split, so it is not a scaffold-held-out test.
facts.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

facts.label: Uncertainty
facts.value: Table 8 reports standard deviations over three replicates. The paper distinguishes this run variation from the choice of molecular dataset and split.
facts.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

facts.value: Molecular dataset and evaluation suite.

facts.label: Organisms

facts.source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

limitations.text: Comparisons must retain the task, split and available structural information. In particular, the two LBA identity thresholds test different generalization regimes.

ops.summary: ATOM3D provides molecular-structure datasets and utilities for task-specific evaluation.
ops.summary_source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: ATOM3D evaluates predictions from molecular structures using eight separate tasks. It supplies task-specific reference labels and partitions, ranging from random small molecules to held-out protein families and future structure-prediction targets. Each task has its own metric and representation-matched baseline; the suite is not a single universal structure score.

facts.label: Datasets
facts.value: Three-dimensional molecular data with associated labels/metadata; ligand-binding affinity is one documented example.
facts.source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

facts.label: Splits
facts.value: Task-specific: random molecules for SMP; 30% protein sequence identity for PIP, MSP and the strict LBA split; CATH topology groups for RES; protein targets for LEP; competition years for PSR and RSR. LBA also provides a less restrictive 60% identity split.
facts.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: SMP: MAE; PIP/MSP/LEP: classification AUROC; RES: accuracy; LBA: RMSE and correlations; PSR/RSR: correlations of predicted structure quality with reference GDT_TS/RMSD. Metrics and aggregation belong to each task.
facts.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

facts.label: Baselines
facts.value: 3D CNNs, graph networks and equivariant networks are compared with task-specific 1D/2D methods; structure-ranking tasks also use established 3D methods. Appendix F documents the per-task comparators.
facts.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: Protein-sequence, topology, target and temporal partitions reduce task-specific overlap; PIP prunes DIPS proteins against DB5. SMP uses a random molecular split, so it is not a scaffold-held-out test.
facts.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

facts.label: Uncertainty
facts.value: Table 8 reports standard deviations over three replicates. The paper distinguishes this run variation from the choice of molecular dataset and split.
facts.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

facts.value: Molecular dataset and evaluation suite.
facts.source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

facts.label: Organisms
facts.value: No single organism defines this suite of molecular structure datasets.
facts.source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

facts.label: Assays
facts.value: Task-specific structural and molecular-property labels.
facts.source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

facts.label: Allowed inputs
facts.value: Three-dimensional molecular coordinates and task labels; supported formats include PDB, SDF and XYZ.
facts.source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

facts.label: Adaptation
facts.value: Supervised task evaluation; task-specific training configurations are linked separately.
facts.source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

strengths.text: Common data loaders allow different 3D representations to use the same dataset definitions.
strengths.source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

limitations.text: Comparisons must retain the task, split and available structural information. In particular, the two LBA identity thresholds test different generalization regimes.

example.summary: Run and evaluate the supplied BEELINE GSD example configuration, then generate AUPRC/AUROC plots.
prerequisites: Git, conda and a functioning Docker installation; the repository executes supported algorithms in containers.
The supplied config-files/config.yaml expects GSD expression, pseudotime and ground-truth files under inputs/example/GSD. Verify the local data layout before running.

steps.title: Check out the reviewed repository
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/Murali-group/Beeline.git
cd Beeline
git checkout --detach 37464085eb8a95d6cc6a3d3a3c649d36db6052ed
steps.explanation: Repository checkout wrapper: the detached revision selects the exact official source inspected for this guide.

steps.title: Set up the environment and algorithm images
steps.shell:
bash utils/setupAnacondaVENV.sh
bash utils/initialize.sh
conda activate BEELINE
steps.explanation: These setup commands use the official default image-pull behavior. Conda must already be initialized in the shell; the README illustrates a Miniconda-specific initialization path.

steps.title: Run the configured algorithms
steps.explanation: This executes the algorithms and datasets enabled by the YAML file. The README points to a missing VSC file; this guide explicitly substitutes the supplied GSD example config, so it is a different example dataset.

steps.title: Evaluate and plot ROC/precision-recall performance
steps.shell:
python BLEvaluator.py -c config-files/config.yaml -a
python BLPlotter.py -c config-files/config.yaml -o ./plots -a -r
steps.explanation: The flags are selected from the official tables: evaluator -a computes AUPRC/AUROC; plotter -a and -r produce their corresponding figures. The README points to a missing VSC file; this guide explicitly substitutes the supplied GSD example config, so it is a different example dataset.

outputs: Ranked edges under outputs/example_run_GSD/GSD/<run_id>/<algorithm_id>/rankedEdges.csv, using output_settings in the supplied config.
AUPRC and AUROC plot files under ./plots in PDF and PNG formats.
limitations: The README VSC command references a configuration absent from the pinned repository. This guide uses the checked-in GSD example instead and does not claim VSC results.
The Docker tags are not image-digest pinned by the README; this code revision alone does not freeze algorithm containers.
Ground-truth network availability and matching input/configuration paths are prerequisites; no data-download command is invented.
The inspected instructions do not establish a minimum RAM/VRAM requirement, wall-clock runtime or monetary cost; none is inferred.

example.title: Download and load an ATOM3D task
example.summary: Install the library and download one of the eight three-dimensional molecular tasks scored on this page.
inputs: A model over three-dimensional atomic structure.
outputs: An LMDB dataset for the chosen task and split.

requirements.data: Downloaded by the library into a local LMDB dataset.
requirements.weights: None. The reported networks are trained from scratch.
requirements.licence: Project licence: MIT. Upstream data licences are separate and unreported here.
requirements.software: Python with the atom3d package from PyPI.
requirements.hardware: Not stated in the cited section. Several of these steps expect a GPU.

instructions.title: Install
instructions.code: pip install atom3d

instructions.code:
import atom3d.datasets as da
da.download_dataset('lba', PATH_TO_DATASET) # Download LBA dataset.

instructions.code:

cases.title: Download and load an ATOM3D task
cases.summary: Install the library and download one of the eight three-dimensional molecular tasks scored on this page.
inputs: A model over three-dimensional atomic structure.
outputs: An LMDB dataset for the chosen task and split.

requirements.data: Downloaded by the library into a local LMDB dataset.
requirements.weights: None. The reported networks are trained from scratch.
requirements.licence: Project licence: MIT. Upstream data licences are separate and unreported here.
requirements.software: Python with the atom3d package from PyPI.
requirements.hardware: Not stated in the cited section. Several of these steps expect a GPU.

instructions.title: Install
instructions.code: pip install atom3d
instructions.source_locator: README.md at 4c2f3b7e, Installation, lines 24-24

instructions.title: Download a dataset
instructions.code:
import atom3d.datasets as da
da.download_dataset('lba', PATH_TO_DATASET) # Download LBA dataset.
instructions.source_locator: README.md at 4c2f3b7e, Downloading a dataset, lines 42-43

instructions.title: Load a dataset
instructions.code:
import atom3d.datasets as da
dataset = da.load_dataset(PATH_TO_DATASET, {'lmdb','pdb','silent','sdf','xyz','xyz-gdb'})
print(len(dataset))  # Print length
print(dataset[0].keys())  # Print keys

example.summary: ATOM3D provides molecular-structure datasets and utilities for task-specific evaluation.
example.summary_source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: ATOM3D evaluates predictions from molecular structures using eight separate tasks. It supplies task-specific reference labels and partitions, ranging from random small molecules to held-out protein families and future structure-prediction targets. Each task has its own metric and representation-matched baseline; the suite is not a single universal structure score.

facts.label: Datasets
facts.value: Three-dimensional molecular data with associated labels/metadata; ligand-binding affinity is one documented example.
facts.source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

facts.label: Splits
facts.value: Task-specific: random molecules for SMP; 30% protein sequence identity for PIP, MSP and the strict LBA split; CATH topology groups for RES; protein targets for LEP; competition years for PSR and RSR. LBA also provides a less restrictive 60% identity split.
facts.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: SMP: MAE; PIP/MSP/LEP: classification AUROC; RES: accuracy; LBA: RMSE and correlations; PSR/RSR: correlations of predicted structure quality with reference GDT_TS/RMSD. Metrics and aggregation belong to each task.
facts.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

facts.label: Baselines
facts.value: 3D CNNs, graph networks and equivariant networks are compared with task-specific 1D/2D methods; structure-ranking tasks also use established 3D methods. Appendix F documents the per-task comparators.
facts.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: Protein-sequence, topology, target and temporal partitions reduce task-specific overlap; PIP prunes DIPS proteins against DB5. SMP uses a random molecular split, so it is not a scaffold-held-out test.
facts.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

facts.label: Uncertainty
facts.value: Table 8 reports standard deviations over three replicates. The paper distinguishes this run variation from the choice of molecular dataset and split.
facts.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

facts.label: Entity type
facts.value: Molecular dataset and evaluation suite.
facts.source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

facts.label: Organisms
facts.value: No single organism defines this suite of molecular structure datasets.
facts.source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

facts.label: Assays
facts.value: Task-specific structural and molecular-property labels.
facts.source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

facts.label: Allowed inputs
facts.value: Three-dimensional molecular coordinates and task labels; supported formats include PDB, SDF and XYZ.
facts.source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

facts.label: Adaptation
facts.value: Supervised task evaluation; task-specific training configurations are linked separately.
facts.source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

strengths.text: Common data loaders allow different 3D representations to use the same dataset definitions.
strengths.source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

limitations.text: Comparisons must retain the task, split and available structural information. In particular, the two LBA identity thresholds test different generalization regimes.

cases.title: Evaluation methodology
cases.body: ATOM3D evaluates predictions from molecular structures using eight separate tasks. It supplies task-specific reference labels and partitions, ranging from random small molecules to held-out protein families and future structure-prediction targets. Each task has its own metric and representation-matched baseline; the suite is not a single universal structure score.
cases.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

cases.label: Datasets
cases.value: Three-dimensional molecular data with associated labels/metadata; ligand-binding affinity is one documented example.
cases.source_locator: Pinned README: Overview; dataset access; supported formats and splitting/filtering utilities

cases.label: Splits
cases.value: Task-specific: random molecules for SMP; 30% protein sequence identity for PIP, MSP and the strict LBA split; CATH topology groups for RES; protein targets for LEP; competition years for PSR and RSR. LBA also provides a less restrictive 60% identity split.
cases.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

cases.label: Metrics
cases.value: SMP: MAE; PIP/MSP/LEP: classification AUROC; RES: accuracy; LBA: RMSE and correlations; PSR/RSR: correlations of predicted structure quality with reference GDT_TS/RMSD. Metrics and aggregation belong to each task.
cases.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

cases.label: Baselines
cases.value: 3D CNNs, graph networks and equivariant networks are compared with task-specific 1D/2D methods; structure-ranking tasks also use established 3D methods. Appendix F documents the per-task comparators.
cases.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

cases.label: Leakage controls
cases.value: Protein-sequence, topology, target and temporal partitions reduce task-specific overlap; PIP prunes DIPS proteins against DB5. SMP uses a random molecular split, so it is not a scaffold-held-out test.
cases.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

cases.label: Uncertainty
cases.value: Table 8 reports standard deviations over three replicates. The paper distinguishes this run variation from the choice of molecular dataset and split.
cases.source_locator: Sections 3.1–3.8, 4–5; Appendix D–F; Table 8

example.summary: AlphaGenome predicts regulatory activity and variant effects from long DNA sequences, with outputs for expression, splicing, chromatin and contact maps.
example.summary_source_locator: Paper: Unifying DNA sequence-to-function model and Discussion; README.md: Model weights and licensing; Supplementary Methods: Model (p.9), ENCODE RNA-seq Data (p.3), Contact maps

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: AlphaGenome progressively downsamples DNA with convolutional blocks, then uses a transformer tower and pairwise interaction blocks to represent long-range context. A U-Net-style decoder restores sequence resolution using skip connections. Modality-specific heads predict one-dimensional genomic tracks, splicing outputs and two-dimensional contact maps.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Unifying DNA sequence-to-function model and Discussion; README.md: Model weights and licensing; Supplementary Methods: Model (p.9), ENCODE RNA-seq Data (p.3), Contact maps

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The paper distinguishes fold-specific evaluation models, all-fold teachers and distilled students; a family name alone does not choose one of these configurations. Up to 1 million base pairs; single-base outputs for the modalities described in the README.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Unifying DNA sequence-to-function model and Discussion; README.md: Model weights and licensing; Supplementary Methods: Model (p.9), ENCODE RNA-seq Data (p.3), Contact maps

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: U-Net-inspired sequence backbone combining convolutional local processing with transformer blocks for longer-range interactions; one-dimensional track heads and two-dimensional contact-map representations.

limitations.text: The paper identifies remaining challenges beyond 100kb, context-specific variant effects and non-coding genes. Species coverage is human/mouse and personal-genome prediction was not benchmarked in the study.

cases.title: How it works
cases.body: AlphaGenome progressively downsamples DNA with convolutional blocks, then uses a transformer tower and pairwise interaction blocks to represent long-range context. A U-Net-style decoder restores sequence resolution using skip connections. Modality-specific heads predict one-dimensional genomic tracks, splicing outputs and two-dimensional contact maps.
cases.source_locator: Paper: Unifying DNA sequence-to-function model and Discussion; README.md: Model weights and licensing; Supplementary Methods: Model (p.9), ENCODE RNA-seq Data (p.3), Contact maps
